requirement:
A paragraph has no declared name. Each prose paragraph has an anonymous
`paragraph` node under its nearest
enclosing outline container. This includes paragraphs before the first heading
and inside list items, quotations, and directive bodies. Their selectors follow
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Heading text and literal
code-block contents create no paragraph nodes. Syntax that has no outline node
is transparent when finding the enclosing container.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.paragraphs` has no implementation roots, and none are needed. It has test edges and no implementation edges. Every clause describes the outline the Markdown source produces, so tests can check it.

I considered each clause as a possible structural obligation:
- "Each prose paragraph has an anonymous `paragraph` node under its nearest enclosing outline container", including paragraphs before the first heading and inside list items, quotations and directive bodies. This fixes the output tree shape and the node kind. An implementation could build that tree with a different parser, a different traversal or different helpers, and the outline would be identical. The clause names no library, algorithm, type or signature.
- "Their selectors follow `requirements.references.outline_selectors`". This is a cited grammar for the output. It constrains the selector strings produced, not how the code is built.
- "Heading text and literal code-block contents create no paragraph nodes". This is an observable exclusion.
- "Syntax that has no outline node is transparent when finding the enclosing container". This is an observable rule for choosing the container.

So every clause specifies observable behavior, and the behavioral tests cover it. No structural obligation needs an `{impl}` reference.

behavioral: The three reviewed tests cover each behavioral obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.paragraphs`.

- **Anonymous `paragraph` nodes under the nearest enclosing container.** `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/markdown_tests.rs` asserts the exact list of (kind, parent, start line, end line) tuples. A paragraph sits under the section, another under the outer `note` block, and a third under the nested `tip` block. This checks the parent assignment and shows that paragraphs in directive bodies get their own nodes.
- **Paragraphs before the first heading and in list items and quotations.** `paragraphs_in_transparent_lists_and_quotes_are_selectable` uses the source "Before heading / - List paragraph / > Quoted paragraph / Title ===== / After heading". It asserts four paragraphs at lines 1, 3, 5 and 10. It asserts that the first three share parent node 1. It asserts that the paragraph after the setext heading is parented to `section[Title]`. This also covers transparent syntax: the list and quote create no nodes, so the paragraphs fall to the enclosing container.
- **Heading text and literal code-block contents create no paragraphs.**
  - The exact node list in the first test has no paragraph for the ATX heading `# Authentication`. It has none for the fenced block's `hi`, which appears only as a `block` node.
  - The second test's paragraph count of exactly 4 excludes a paragraph for the setext heading text `Title`.
- **Selectors follow `requirements.references.outline_selectors`.** The first test checks that every node's selector resolves back to its own index. It checks that each non-section segment has the form `paragraph@` plus 12 characters. It checks that `node_lines` matches the source range. `anonymous_identities_survive_reflow_and_sibling_edits_and_number_duplicates` checks that selectors are stable under reflow and sibling edits. It checks that the structural hash changes when content changes. It checks that duplicate paragraphs are numbered `#1` and `#2`.

I found no required behavior that these assertions would let a violating implementation pass. The tests also carry `{test}` markers for the subject. I did not examine indented code blocks or code with blank lines, because the requirement does not name them.
